safety_description: This issue needs attention within the next 1-2 weeks. Your vehicle is safe for short trips, but the problem will get worse or more expensive if ignored.
dont_panic: Your 2022 Ram 3500 is showing code P0420. This means the catalytic converter, which reduces harmful emissions, is not working efficiently. The vehicle’s own readings show the converter is well past its manufacturer limit (measured 0.9 against a limit of 0.5). This is not a temporary issue—it indicates the converter is genuinely worn out. The engine is running at idle with 22% load and 195°F coolant temperature, which are normal for this condition. Mileage data was not available.
likely_causes: 1. The catalytic converter is worn out and no longer meets the manufacturer’s efficiency standards. Evidence: the catalyst monitor measured 0.9 against a manufacturer limit of 0.5.
symptoms:
1. Reduced fuel efficiency — the converter’s failure can make the engine work harder.
2. The check engine light staying on — this is a direct indicator of the issue.
3. A smell of burning or sulfur — a sign of incomplete fuel combustion.
4. Rough idling or hesitation — the engine may struggle to run smoothly.
if_ignored: The converter could fail completely, leading to more expensive repairs. Over time, the engine may suffer damage from unburned fuel. Emissions could exceed legal limits, risking fines. Long-term, the vehicle may fail to pass emissions tests or experience reduced performance.
quick_checks: - Get a replacement quote; confirm no upstream fault remains.
diy_fix: This repair is NOT recommended for DIY because it requires specialized tools and expertise to diagnose and replace the catalytic converter safely. A professional mechanic should handle this.
urgency: Try to get this looked at in the next few days. Driving short trips is fine, but do not delay repairs.
repair_cost:
Parts: $500 - $1,200 (catalytic converter varies by quality).
Labor: $300 - $600 (depending on shop).
Total at independent shop: $800 - $1,800.
Total at dealer: $1,000 - $2,200 (dealers charge more).
